# Onsite BQ + Hiring Manager + Project Deep-Dive

[← Uber](../README.md) · [Every Uber question](../../uber.md) · [Read it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/study/onsite-bq-hm-deep-dive)

`deep-dive` `presentation`

---

## Requirements

- **Project deep-dive (30–45 min)** — choose one resume project and explain its architecture, major choices, your individual work, and the resulting metrics. Recruiters frequently **proactively offer** the option of using slides for this portion; several candidates have described that as a notable benefit.
- **Structured BQ (15–30 min)** — common prompts include:
  - What was your team’s scope, how was the organization arranged, and which metrics did you own?
  - How would you manage someone performing poorly? (manager candidates only.)
  - Describe a disagreement with your manager or with a cross-functional colleague (PM, DS, or design).
  - How have you mentored others, established a roadmap, or settled conflict between teams?
  - "Describe the occasion when you had the greatest impact on your team."
- For L5+ / Senior IC: clear evidence of cross-functional influence and mentorship is expected; saying "I delivered X more quickly" does not suffice.
- For Staff (L6 / BPS): this round is divided into **Scope & Impact** and **Architecture** — refer to the dedicated BPS card.

## Notes

- **Preparing slides is the highest-leverage move.** Limit the deck to 5–7 slides covering the problem, your role, the architecture, key decisions, results, and lessons learned. Present for less than 25 minutes to leave room for interviewer questions.
- The HM places particular emphasis on **leadership and cross-functional collaboration**. Candidates have failed this round despite having a technically strong project when they discussed only technical complexity and omitted cross-functional work, mentorship, and business results.
- Typical deep-dive follow-ups include:
  - "Which parts of this project were outside your ownership, and who owned them?"
  - "What would you change if you did it again?"
  - "How did you define success, and what was the starting baseline?"
  - "How did you balance X against Y?"
- Prepare 2–3 STAR stories in advance covering a challenging cross-team partner, a technical disagreement on which you later changed your position, and a project that missed its deadline.

- The HM round explicitly evaluates **influence without authority** and **scope of impact** — responses focused on one deliverable, without identifying a cross-functional partner, mentee, or measurable business outcome, are regularly rated borderline. Open each STAR story with the partner, mentee, or metric rather than the technical details.

## Preparation

- Create the slide deck in advance, even when the recruiter has not requested one — it is offered roughly 60% of the time for L5+ candidates. Use a lightweight PDF without embedded video.
- Rehearse three STAR stories that demonstrate different signals: cross-functional work, mentorship, and conflict. Keep each one to 2–3 minutes.
- Manager / EM candidates should prepare an example of handling a low performer, whether through a PIP, coaching, or eventual departure — this is asked directly.
- Practice a 90-second elevator pitch on team scope, including the org chart, your metrics, and the roadmap for the next six months. Recruiters say it appears in the first five minutes roughly 70% of the time and establishes the context for the rest of the interview.

- Recent senior loops still divide the round approximately evenly between the project deep-dive and standard behavioral questions. Interviewers assess ownership, communication, conflict management, and how well you can explain complicated project decisions to an HM audience.
